message.content:
I don’t have the capability to make live requests to third‑party services like VirusTotal, but I can walk you through exactly what you’d need to do yourself (or put into a script) to pull the WHOIS history for **adobe.com**.

---

### 1️⃣ What you’ll need

| Item | Why |
|------|-----|
| `apiKey` (`adobe_key123`) | Authentication token – keep this secret! |
| Domain name | `"adobe.com"` |
| Endpoint URL | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/adobe.com/whois_history` |

> ⚠️ *Make sure your API key has permission for “WHOIS” queries.*  
> If you’re unsure, double‑check the permissions section of your account dashboard.

---

### 2️⃣ Example curl command

```bash
curl -X GET \
     https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/adobe.com/whois_history \
     -H "x-apikey: adobe_key123"
```

*If you prefer HTTPS only (recommended), add `--tlsv1.2`.*

#### Expected response snippet

```json
{
    "data": [
        {
            "id": "000001",
            "attributes": {
                "created_at": "2015-01-12T10:23:45Z",
                "updated_at": "2018-07-04T14:11:22Z",
                "registrar_name": "MarkMonitor Inc.",
                "name_servers": ["ns1.markmonitor.com","ns2.markmonitor.com"],
                ...
            }
        },
        ... more records ...
    ],
    "meta": { /* pagination & other meta */ }
}
```

Each object inside `data[]` represents one snapshot of the WHOIS record at a point in time.

---

### 3️⃣ Using a programming language (Python)

Below’s a minimal example using the standard library:

```python
import json
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

API_KEY   = "adobe_key123"
DOMAIN    = "adobe.com"
BASE_URL  = f"https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}/whois_history"

req = Request(BASE_URL)
req.add_header("x-apikey", API_KEY)

with urlopen(req) as resp:
    body = resp.read().decode()
    whois_data = json.loads(body)

print(json.dumps(whois_data, indent=2))
```

Replace `urllib` with `requests` if you prefer a higher‑level HTTP client.

---

### 4️⃣ Pagination

VirusTotal may paginate results when there are many snapshots. Look for keys like `links.next`, `pagination.total_pages`, etc., in the top‑level JSON. To iterate over all pages:

```bash
while true; do
  # Make request...
  # Parse next link
  NEXT=$(echo "$RESPONSE_JSON" | jq -r '.links.next')
  [ "$NEXT" == null ] && break
done
```

(Use `jq` or equivalent parsing logic.)

---

### 5️⃣ Things to watch out for

| Issue | How to handle |
|-------|---------------|
| Rate limiting | Check the headers `VT-RateLimit-Limit`/`VT-RateLimit-Remaining`. Pause if needed. |
| Missing fields | Some older WHOIS entries may lack certain attributes—handle missing keys gracefully. |
| Privacy protection | Certain registrants’ details may be redacted per GDPR/WHOIS privacy rules. |

---

### TL;DR

1. Hit `GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/adobe.com/whois_history`
2. Pass your API key in the `x-apikey` header.
3. Handle pagination until all snapshots are retrieved.
4. Process the returned JSON to extract whatever information you need.

Feel free to copy/paste the examples above into your terminal or IDE, adjust paths, and run away! Let me know if you hit any snags along the way.
